inputs.text: I heard about this story from JFK International Airport in New York on Thursday involving an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent who stepped in to help a baby that stopped breathing while with his family in a crowded TSA line. The Department of Homeland Security released video footage of the agent holding the child and taking immediate action. But trying to use this to demand more support for law enforcement and border institutions while dismissing progressive calls for change completely misses the point. It actually draws attention to the structural inequalities and pressures that put vulnerable families in these chaotic, high-risk situations in the first place. We need real institutional reform focused on equity, protection of marginalized groups, and addressing historical patterns of discrimination rather than doubling down on enforcement systems that often expose people to harm.
